clauses.reason: The operative sentence at chars 1114–1312 exempts McNeir and continues him until November 1, 1936. This limits the whole personal grant; the statute quotation, previous exemption recital and signature are not independent commands. The stated day is included through its end; the exclusive alternative ends the grant when November 1 begins. Read ACTOR_TEXT:EO:7477 recites the prior grants and makes a new exemption under section 204 until May 1, 1937. Its October 24, 1936 signing is a later grant event, not proof of separation or an amendment of EO 7205.

research_rationale:
Read ORIGINAL:EO:7205 and ACTOR_TEXT:EO:7477 completely, together with the complete held Photius EO 7205 text. The selected representation's October 14, 1936 signing line conflicts with its supplied 1935 metadata. This is resolved as an OCR date discrepancy for provisional identification: the read Photius text says October 14, 1935, and EO 7477 independently names EO 7205 of October 14, 1935. The selected closing number and subject agree; its bytes are preserved, not silently corrected. November 1, 1936 is consistently the operative terminal date. EO 7477's recital of earlier grants and new performative exemption supply no strike-and-insert, revocation or shortening of this term. The alternative that it extends EO 7205 to May 1, 1937 is rejected because its command grants anew rather than changing EO 7205. Earlier death, retirement or separation is neither documented nor inferred; potential nonuse of a personal exemption does not itself repeal its fixed permission. The inventory is one grant, covering both exemption and continuance. The name-search hit is fully examined as EO 7477. Other selected searches supply bounded counterevidence only: the OFR catalog lacks pre-1937 coverage, USC ends October 9, 2026, and the name corpus omits unheld orders. These limitations do not establish cessation; the express calendar term does. No affirmative contrary lead remains. Same-family AI production; human certification is false and independent whole-case review remains necessary.
